title: SRE shift heuristics + autoscaling trigger review — week of 2026-11-29
body:
Purpose and scope:
This doc captures the SRE weekly sync (2026-11-29) focused on shift heuristics, recent incident patterns, and a targeted review of autoscaling trigger thresholds. Objective: reduce 'capacity shortfall' incidents during unpredictable burst workloads while keeping request-latency SLOs intact.

Attendees:
- Maya Chen (notes, lead)
- Carlos Rivera (on-call rotation coordinator)
- Aisha Patel (serving runtime eng)
- Jon Park (platform infra, autoscaler)
- Paige Liu (observability)

Summary of recent incident trends (last 21 days):
- INC-2026-11-26-cache-thundering: a customer workload caused many near-simultaneous cold-starts on shared KV caching layer; latency spikes for 15 minutes, partial degradation in hosted-api region-us-west2. Root cause: client-side retry amplification + cache TTL misconfiguration. Impact: 0.8% national availability drop for 15m, error-budget burn: 0.04% of 30d.
- INC-2026-11-18-burst-queue-backpressure: autoscaler delayed scale-up because scale decision looked at 1m window; queue depth increased faster than decision cadence. Impact: per-route p95 latency exceeded SLO for 7 minutes.
- Pattern observed: both incidents share a rapid delta in instantaneous load that outpaces a single metric window or causes amplifying retries.

SLO snapshot (team view):
- Text-generation API availability (region us-west2) 7d: 99.92% (SLO target 99.95%).
- P95 latency (inference) 7d: 210ms (SLO target 200ms).
- Error budget remaining (30d rolling): 86%.
- Observability note: the p95 degradation aligns tightly with increases in queue depth and a shortfall in warm-KV-hit-rate.

Hypothesis / working theory:
- The autoscaler and warmup heuristics are tuned for gradual ramps, not for sub-60s step traffic increases combined with client retries.
- The cache warm path and cache-TTL interactions lead to localized hotspots; autoscaler decisions based on averaged CPU and pod count miss very short-lived CPU bursts.

Proposed shift heuristics (operational play):
1) Fast-path alerting for shift-handoff: if a shift handoff occurs within 30m of a scale event or an incident (pager), the incoming on-call must shadow for 30 minutes and mark the handoff as "hot" in the handoff doc. Rationale: we observed multiple mid-handoff escalations.
2) Handoff checklist addition: always surface last 60m autoscaler events, recent scaling decisions, and any manual overrides in the last 24h.
3) Escalation cadence: if p95 > SLO for >5m and queue depth is doubled vs baseline, escalate to platform on-call within 3 minutes.

Autoscaling trigger review (decisions and experiments):
- Current baseline: scale decisions use a 60s moving average of request_rate per pod and CPU utilization, with cooldown 120s.
- Problem: rapid bursts cause queue backlog before the 60s window reflects the spike.
- Short-term experiment (A/B on us-west2):
  * Branch A (pilot, 2a hosts): add an instantaneous request-rate spike detector that triggers an emergency scale-up if request_rate per pod exceeds 4x baseline in a 10s window. Cooldown 30s.
  * Branch B (control, 2b hosts): keep current logic but reduce cooldown from 120s -> 90s and enable predictive warmup flag for known bursty customers.
- Jon to deploy Branch A to 2a and monitor impact for 72h. Carlos to rotate these hosts between on-call pools so incident exposure is limited.

Runbook updates (items to author and priority):
- RU-01: "Emergency autoscale trigger checklist" — include clear rollback steps for false-positive scale-ups. Owner: Jon Park. Due: 2026-12-06.
- RU-02: "Cache-thundering mitigations" — explicit pattern identification: high cold-miss rate + client retry amplification within 30s. Include fixlets: increase hot-set TTL, sticky-client suggestions, circuit-breaker guidance. Owner: Aisha Patel. Due: 2026-12-03.
- RU-03: "Shift hot-hand-off template" — add fields for 'last scale events', 'hot routes', 'recent config changes'. Owner: Carlos Rivera. Due: 2026-12-02.

Instrumentation and dashboards required:
- New heatmap: per-route 10s request-rate ratio (instantaneous vs 60s avg) to surface spikes. Owner: Paige Liu. ETA: 2026-12-08.
- Add a 'recent-scaler-actions' lane to the SRE console with last 10 scaling decisions and cooldown states. Owner: Jon Park. ETA: 2026-12-07.

Action items (owners and due dates):
- Jon Park: deploy Branch A pilot autoscaler logic to 2a hosts, add feature flag for emergency scale detector. Monitor for 72h and report. Due: 2026-12-02.
- Aisha Patel: produce RU-02 draft (cache mitigations), include exemplar client-side retry guidance. Due: 2026-12-03.
- Carlos Rivera: update handoff template and circulate to SRE rotation. Due: 2026-12-02.
- Paige Liu: prototype per-route 10s heatmap dashboard and attach to the weekly SRE console. Due: 2026-12-08.
- Maya Chen: run a 30m tabletop handoff drill next Tue to validate 'hot' handoff flow; invite platform on-call and a runtime lead. Due: 2026-12-01.

Risks and guardrails:
- Emergency scale detector false positives could increase cloud spend; mitigate with immediate cooldown and a budget guard flag that prevents scale beyond N nodes without human approval during pilot.
- Cache TTL changes may affect memory footprint; coordinate with infra cost owners before global rollout.

Open questions / discussion points for next sync:
- What is the acceptable cost delta for reducing SLO p95 breaches caused by rapid bursts? (Quantify in $/day for leadership.)
- Do we want to implement route-level rate limit recommendations for high-burst customers as a product change or keep as SRE advisory?
- How to surface cross-region fallback decisions automatically in the handoff doc?

Meeting notes / raw chatter (abridged):
- Carlos: "We've been burned twice where the handoff owner didn't see the scale event list — small UI change would help."
- Jon: "Emergency detector looks sane in simulation, but we need guardrails to avoid flare-ups."
- Aisha: "Cache TTL knobs exist in service X, but we should expose a warm-up API for dedicated customers."

Follow-ups:
- Weekly sync will re-open this topic on 2026-12-06 at 10:00 PT to review pilot metrics.
- Add this doc to rotation onboarding checklist for the next two rotations.

Appendix (incident quick details):
- INC-2026-11-26-cache-thundering: pager fired at 03:11 PT, mitigation applied at 03:25 PT (temporary TTL bump and emergency client throttling rule), full recovery 03:27 PT. Postmortem draft link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/INC-2026-11-26
- INC-2026-11-18-burst-queue-backpressure: pager at 14:04 PT, root cause: scale cooldown and averaged metric. Auto-mitigation: manual scale to 3x capacity at 14:09 PT.

If you are assigned an action above and your calendar conflicts prevent delivery, please reassign within 24h and ping #sre-ops.

End of notes.
